_meta.purpose: Grading rubric for evaluating candidates' resumes and public footprint (GitHub, blog, LinkedIn, Kaggle, etc.) per job position.

dimension_notes.technical_competency: Role-specific: depth of hard/technical skills relevant to the position.
dimension_notes.problem_solving: Role-specific: evidence of tackling non-trivial technical problems in that domain.
dimension_notes.communication: Universal: clarity of writing (README, docs, articles), ability to explain technical concepts, quality of resume narrative.
dimension_notes.career_stability: Universal: tenure patterns, frequency of job changes, unexplained gaps, progression logic.
dimension_notes.company_exposure: Universal (lightly role-flavored): caliber, scale, and relevance of past employers.
dimension_notes.academic_signal: Universal (lightly role-flavored): relevance and strength of formal education, certifications, coursework.
dimension_notes.initiative: Universal: self-driven learning, side projects, open-source contributions, competitions, community involvement.
dimension_notes.risk_indicators: Universal, INVERTED scale — higher score = LOWER risk. Captures red flags: fabrication, plagiarism, erratic job hopping, inconsistent claims, inactivity, unexplained employment gaps, unprofessional public conduct.
dimension_notes.role_domain_relevance: Role-specific: how much of the candidate's demonstrated work/portfolio actually sits inside this role's domain.

technical_competency.90-100: Demonstrates mastery of server-side languages (Python, Go, Node.js, Java), database architecture (SQL/NoSQL), microservices, API design, and strong CI/CD automation.
technical_competency.70-89: Solid understanding of backend frameworks and database operations, but lacks advanced system design or automation.
technical_competency.50-69: Can build basic REST endpoints and use an ORM, but shows limited grasp of scalability, security, or data modeling.
technical_competency.30-49: Only exposure via tutorials/bootcamp projects; no evidence of independent backend architecture decisions.
technical_competency.0-29: No credible evidence of backend skills, or claims are inconsistent with any visible code/projects.

problem_solving.90-100: Evidence of solving complex scalability, concurrency, distributed-systems, or performance bottleneck problems (e.g. caching strategy, queueing, sharding).
problem_solving.70-89: Can implement standard CRUD features and resolve typical bugs; some evidence of optimizing queries or fixing production issues.
problem_solving.50-69: Solves problems only at tutorial/toy-project complexity; little evidence of debugging real systems.
problem_solving.30-49: Minimal problem-solving evidence; mostly boilerplate or copied code patterns.
problem_solving.0-29: No evidence of independent problem-solving ability.

communication.90-100: Writes clear, well-structured READMEs/technical docs/API specs; may have published articles explaining backend concepts; resume clearly narrates technical decisions and impact.
communication.70-89: Adequate documentation on projects; resume is clear but light on explaining trade-offs or decisions.
communication.50-69: Sparse documentation; resume is generic/templated with little technical narrative.
communication.30-49: Minimal or confusing documentation; unclear resume descriptions.
communication.0-29: No documentation, or communication is incoherent/contradictory.

career_stability.90-100: Clear, logical career progression with tenures typically 2+ years per role and sensible reasons for transitions.
career_stability.70-89: Mostly stable history with one or two shorter stints that have plausible explanations.
career_stability.50-69: Mixed pattern: some short tenures (<1 year) without clear explanation, or one unexplained gap.
career_stability.30-49: Frequent job-hopping (multiple <1 year roles) or multiple unexplained gaps.
career_stability.0-29: Highly erratic history, chronic short tenures, or unexplained long gaps with no context.

company_exposure.90-100: Experience at well-known, engineering-strong companies (large-scale tech companies, high-growth startups with strong backend/infra needs) in relevant backend/infra roles.
company_exposure.70-89: Experience at reputable mid-size companies or startups with legitimate engineering functions.
company_exposure.50-69: Experience mostly at small/unknown companies or in generalist/non-engineering-heavy roles.
company_exposure.30-49: Very limited or unclear company exposure; roles not clearly technical.
company_exposure.0-29: No verifiable company exposure, or roles unrelated to software engineering.

academic_signal.90-100: Degree in CS/Software Engineering/related field from a recognized institution, and/or strong relevant certifications (cloud, databases, systems design).
academic_signal.70-89: Relevant degree from a lesser-known institution, or unrelated degree plus solid relevant certifications.
academic_signal.50-69: Unrelated degree with minimal relevant coursework/certification.
academic_signal.30-49: No formal degree; only short/basic online courses.
academic_signal.0-29: No academic signal at all, or credentials appear unverifiable/fabricated.

initiative.90-100: Active open-source contributions, personal backend/infra side projects, blog posts, or participation in relevant hackathons/competitions.
initiative.70-89: Some side projects or occasional contributions, but not sustained.
initiative.50-69: A couple of forked/copied repos with minimal original work.
initiative.30-49: Barely any public activity beyond required coursework/job tasks.
initiative.0-29: No initiative evidence at all; entirely passive profile.

risk_indicators.90-100: No red flags: consistent story across resume/LinkedIn/GitHub, active and authentic public presence, no plagiarism or fabricated claims.

risk_indicators.0-29: Clear red flags: fabricated experience, plagiarized code/projects, contradictory claims, or unprofessional conduct visible publicly.
